routes.label: Connect the circle angles to a triangle

question:
Points \(A,\) \(B,\) \(Q,\) \(D,\) and \(C\) lie on the circle shown, and the measures of arcs \(BQ\) and \(QD\) are \(42^\circ\) and \(38^\circ,\) respectively. The sum of the measures of angles \(P\) and \(Q\) is:

[Figure 1](figures/1971_AMC_12_Q05_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Draw chord \(BC\). This creates triangle \(PBC\), allowing us to relate the angle at \(P\) to an angle determined by the given arcs.

The diagram has \(P,A,B\) collinear in that order and \(P,C,D\) collinear in that order. Thus \(\angle PBC=\angle ABC\). The inscribed angles \(ABC\) and \(AQC\) intercept the same arc \(AC\), so
\[
\angle PBC=\angle AQC.
\]
Also, \(\angle BCD\) intercepts the arc from \(B\) through \(Q\) to \(D\). By the inscribed angle theorem,
\[
\angle BCD=\frac{42^\circ+38^\circ}{2}=40^\circ.
\]
Because \(CD\) extends side \(CP\), angle \(BCD\) is an exterior angle of triangle \(PBC\). It equals the sum of the two remote interior angles, giving
\[
\angle BPC+\angle AQC
=\angle BPC+\angle PBC
=40^\circ.
\]
The requested sum is therefore \(\boxed{40^\circ}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
